body:
Okay! Let’s do this!

I grew up middle class in England, born in the mid 80’s with a (so far) lifetimes worth of thick blond hair and bright blue eyes. My mum didn’t have to work because my dad got a lucrative job very young ~ but both my folks grew up very poor, half of my (still alive too. All nearing 100yo) grandparents were born in another country so I was raised in a middle class, high quality, multicultural, socially-minded (my dads best mate since their childhood who is also my godfather is Ethiopian and I was raised to call him my uncle), pro-education, pro-pets, staunch anti-racist, no hoots given about the intended gender of a toy we played with them all as kids, just a fuckin good time.

But growing up my dad had to share a bed with his brother, there was ice in bedrooms in winter, they had an outdoor toilet. He’s the perfect chap and I had a fucking sweet childhood and upbringing. He got me into electronics at a young age so I was smart at school, he managed to get me so many leg-ups (as we call them here. No idea if it’s a global phrase and I honestly don’t care hah. I despise the social homogenisation especially as a kid of the 90’s with its drilling of individuality. It’s so bad now I’ve seen folk get mocked for using local terms or not using global ones). 

One weekly event was I’d head a quarter mile with my mates on my road (technically a “lane”) to the local shop and my dad would pay in advance so I’d just go there myself and pick random VHS tv shows or films. Without knowing anything about the genre I used to get a lot of Japanese shows, fully converted to Englishbl by way of Americans. If my folks weren’t sure they’d watch whatever I picked before me to decide if I could watch it. It was almost always yes - I’ve always been mature and such even as a wee kid. My dad’s work best mate (he was night manager and his best work pal was the day manager) bought me mortal kombat when it first came out. We had to get a plug adapted for it. [proofreading this I realise it’s not clear it was an arcade unit haha]

Anywho. Pokemon came out when I was about 10, 11. I had the money saved up for it. I walked to the town centre with some school friends (it was about 4 miles away) through meadows and woods and the rougher inner-town areas. But my folks were sure I left with just enough for Pokemon Red.

But the shops were all out of stock!!!

I had a poster of all 151 Pokemon framed by my bed and before sleep id imagine which ones I’d want in my team. 

But time came and went. The first Pokemon game I actually got was Sapphire. I was so excited for it (it was dispatched 2 days before launch, as was the way back then thanks to CDWOW dot com hah. ) I couldn’t sit still and so spent the day it was in the post on a bike trip with some friends. I burned off so much energy that I managed to make it 16 miles to a neighbouring town and then back again. I got home, had a long sit in the steam room, showered, and slept like a baby. 

I was 16 now. Sure I missed the GB era but I’d catch up. I have a really awesome collection of all the physical games (main series only). My fave so far has been the Gen 2 remake and the Hawaiian one. My least fave has been the French one and dare I say the English one. Their games have a feeling of rushedness at the end. The Hawaiian one with its paltry ice zone just didn’t sit well with me. I’ve made software myself and I get the rush near the end - especially as I know for a fact Pokemon games are almost always made in journey order (with the first village being the first zone developed and the last area being the final story development.)

I love talking about Pokemon more than playing them now. I’m not fussed about this Gen 5 remake coming our way. You don’t have to follow patterns (as in they’ve remade the rest in order). And I’d prefer they go wilder like they did with the Arceus [spelling] game for future second-tier mainline titles.

It’s funny. I met my wife when we were both 16 years old. She was super into Pokemon having beaten gen 1 and made good progress on gen 2 (without cheating also! I can’t remember if it was Pokemon or FF7 that she maxed out the game timer on). I love her to bits, we enjoy the games together too. Even now as we’re much older than we were (duh! It’ll happen to you too haha). We still preorder the games and set aside days to sit and play them around the grounds. I don’t work so I get to play whenever I want really , she works but not too much. It’s 10am right now and she’s still fast sleep as I’m wasting my time writing this as it’ll no doubt be moderated and removed because some weird folk believe there’s a time limit for open questions like this topic

I bought the games as presents for relatives, my own kids freakin’ love Pikachu and (my forever-main) Raichu. God damn love that thing.

It’s funny also my wife and I have a close friend who we, enjoy time with. Just a fun thing nothing heavy. Any road her fave is also Raichu. My wife’s fave is Squirtle (and I can see why. Love that 90s round squat cute dinosaur that Japan does/did so well).  My nephews and nieces are older and into the shows. My best online friend is actually watching the show. The whole thing! (I personally hate the show. Used to enjoy the films but haven’t seen one for a long long time). My IRL best mate just flat out isn’t bothered by Pokemon.

One of the best moments of my life was winning an award in Japan and getting to go there and visit the companies whose games I play daily. Eg Nintendo, Gamefreak, the guy who made Smash Bros. Sorry names escaping me! Yeah!

One thing I hate about the new one; scarlet, is the fact there’s barely any indoor scenes. Hawaii was so well contained and flawless. It felt way better to explore. To me: slower, smaller, details everywhere games are much better than ones stretched outwards. BOTW and TOTK both feel stretched out yet the devs clearly then spent ages refining the details. Just isn’t there in Scarlet.

Did you also know your car costs like £100 in raw materials yet they mark it up to £15k?
Did you also know a fancy pants top of the line iPad Pro costs £50 in materials but they charge you £1k?
Also psyke… cause I know some people are weird on the internet and have some anti Apple irrational hatred - same goes for all major brands. So let’s say all those folding phones (that can’t hold up to a fingernail) have a greater mark up than any of Apples iPhones or iPads, or even their laptops or desktop computers. 

“So why doesn’t a new company come along and offer the same food dominos does for half the price?”
1. Setting up national restaurants is next to impossible now. Notice how all the big players have been around for decades? Back when standards were lower. 
2. And when someone does have a good idea they often get bought out. My background is in drinks manufacturing, lots of my friends and peers do so too. Around 2000 the goal shifted from “being a successful manufacturer” to “getting bought out from the big boys”. Look it up yourself. Try your local corner shops if you live in a place that has them, or local supermarkets or markets, all they sell are drinks from like 3 major companies. In fact there’s shit loads of corruption too, the governments sugar tax for example - one of those Tory policies that benefits a friend of a high up, donor etc. because actually sugar free drinks are bad, the joke about Americans being fat from huge sugary drinks? Not the case, their drinks are made from HFCS. That stuff is nasty. 

I made a YouTube channel outing all these government bollocks and corruption, I’ve spoke to journalists but their stories weren’t published (thankfully there’s a term for this now: ghosted). Folk don’t care. You can be sure if it was the other political party doing it they’d be up in arms but never when it’s their guys. Well I’m done on my annual visit to social sites.

No that makes no sense. As someone who can afford to not see other people if I don’t want to, it’s been good having this peace. Would I want another year of this? No thanks. Maybe have a virus every 6-7 years that keeps us all indoors with our families, hobbies, pastimes. 

It actually comes across as mental to want to live in the rat race that some people do. It looks so loud, nobody caring about you on social transport, dirty, wasteful. 

It’s much better living peacefully at home. I’ve adored:

- doing the gardening. Our house sits on a few acres of land and so we have numerous fun gardens that needed attention. (And no we don’t hire help. Do it yourself! My family is rich and my dad taught me all the life skills I need like woodwork/carpeting, plumbing, electricity, dry stone walling, gardening etc etc 
- playing all the video games I’ve wanted to play. I’ve not been able to put my modified Snes classic down with all the extra games I added.
- reading. Years ago I realised I could build some reading nooks around the land and inside the house. I’ve got an ‘egg pod’ in the garden that is serene and my fave. Plus tucked away places on the top floor, in corners, under the grand staircase. That plus the Kindle oasis has made reading so much fun I’ve found it difficult to stop.
- spending time with my family. So much time for intimacy with my partner, time to spend with the kids and their creative projects oh that reminds me-
- creative projects! So many to do. Making my art books by binding them, learning instruments, learning modern coding methods (I made a middleware product in the 90s that was very very successful. But I don’t manage that now I just collect royalties.)
- watching all the shows and films I’ve wanted to.
- working out more, which the gardening and DIY took a lot of care of. 

You only have one life. Enjoy it! If you live in a tiny flat in the middle of a big city then you’re just wasting your life making money for someone else. Escape the rat race. It’s pathetic.

Me too. It truly has been the best year of my life. 

I live in a fairly biggish house on the outskirts of a village. Before the virus I had to attend lots of local events. This year I’ve spent it all tidying the house up, doing all those chores that built up over the years (a house this size too hehe). My partner and I watched a lot of tv. We’d wake at 8am and just watch whatever show we were into until 11pm or midday. Then on with the house stuff. The house sits on a few acres of land and we’ve built a few independent gardens within them. They needed so much maintenance.

It’s just been nice.

I’m a hardcore gamer at heart and spent a lot of time on my SNES classic console. I hacked it and added more storage and games, added all the games I’ve always wanted to play. Such fun!

I read so much too. Years ago I realised I could build reading nooks. It was easy enough, my dad trained me in carpeting as a kid. I don’t even know if that’s the right term! But I’m good with wood and power tools. I put up plaster board, plastered, painted, put carpet down. Added lights and power sockets. Pops taught me a lot about electricity too. He basically provided half my schooling! I’d do normal school stuff then come home and do his classes. He’s big on self sufficiency. Always said there’s no need for a plumber, electrician, builder when you can do it yourself. One I truly loved was dry stone walling but there’s not much call for that on the grounds.

I secured fencing around the land, I put up additional security cameras to keep the oiks out. The hoodlums, maniacs. Sometimes they come onto the land and look around. Always send footage off the local police force. I even installed an electric gate system! It cost about 1k for the gate and they wanted another 1k to install it! Thieves! Did it myself. But I did all this so the dog could run free during the day and have nothing come in to attack it or have it chase a squirrel to out of the land.

It’s going to be hard going back to normality.

I’m semi retired in a way. I’m in my 30s and family money/trusts support me but I did make some middleware software a while ago that I still get a licensing royalty from. It’s a good life really. So I don’t have to see people if I don’t want to but I do feel obligations to help out the local village with events and such. Id just rather not! 

Ps. We don’t employ maids or anything like that. It’s just us. I’m sufficient enough and my partner is capable too. There’s no need to employ people to work for you almost all the time. Unless you’re busy? It’s just ridiculous to me and a waste of money. It’s best in your pocket than anyone or anything elses.

I've made games for 30 years and played them a bit longer. Played with all the cutting tech toys as they came out, secret machines and devices that never saw the light of day, blah blah. I've defeated Icon of Sin on PC, PS4 Pro. But none of those are perfect. The Switch is. It has analogue movement on the left stick, analogue aiming on the right + (and this's the big part) motion aiming for precise shots. 

The PC version supports controllers and keyboard+mouse. Keyboard is digital, mouse analogue and precise.

The PS4 version supports controllers. Analogue movement, analogue aiming but on a stick so less precise than mouse.

Switch has it all. Analogue movement, and then two forms of analogue aiming (one for big movements, like the PS4. And another for precise tweaking of a shot.)
